digest.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro reaches 55 on the AA index, Meta's Muse Wonder Full ties Sonnet 5.5 at 56, Gemini 4 Argon goes GA, and Anthropic launches Claude Duet
digest.summary: The frontier got crowded over the past two weeks. Meta's Muse Wonder Full (Oct 12) scores 56 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, level with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and two points behind Opus 5.5. Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro (Oct 23) scores 55, an 11-point jump over K3, with open weights promised by November 4; Artificial Analysis says that would cut the open-vs-closed gap to 3 points. Google made Gemini 4 Argon (AA 53) generally available on October 13. Anthropic opened a waitlist for Claude Duet, a proactive background agent on Opus 5.5, and published research in which Claude proved 239 entry points across 123 open-source libraries crash-free at the binary level, finding hundreds of bugs along the way. Microsoft says a China-aligned group used the ARTEX agentic pentest framework to reach 2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants through compromised ConnectWise apps, and OpenAI is reportedly raising up to $30B at a $1.25T valuation. Tooling: Claude Code reached 2.1.310 (Monitor tool on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry), Codex 0.164.0 adds `/presets` and inline `/model` arguments, and Pi 1.4.0 queues codemode workers instead of failing.

stories.title: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 55 on the AA index, fourth overall
stories.dek: Released October 23, K3.1 Pro is a 2.8T-parameter mixture-of-experts model (104B active) with a 1M-token context and text and image input. Artificial Analysis scores it 55, 11 points above Kimi K3 and behind only Opus 5.5 (58), Sonnet 5.5 (56), and Muse Wonder Full (56). Moonshot cut API prices by a third to $2/$10 per million input/output tokens ($0.20 cached); a 2–3x faster Highspeed variant costs $4/$20. Moonshot reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and says full weights will ship by November 4.
stories.whyItMatters: Once the weights ship, it should be the strongest open-weights model by a wide margin, at a fraction of Opus pricing. Moonshot's benchmark claims beyond the AA index haven't been independently verified yet.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive background agent, as a research preview
stories.dek: Announced October 21, Duet runs on Claude Opus 5.5 and watches your connected apps. It sends a morning brief and takes tasks by text or voice, from scheduling meetings to building forecasts. It drafts and prepares work on its own, but shows you what it's about to do and waits for approval before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything. A separate classifier screens outgoing messages for sensitive data. The waitlist is open to US Pro and Max subscribers on iOS, Android, and claude.ai. It costs nothing extra during the preview, but its background work counts toward plan limits.
stories.whyItMatters: Anthropic is now competing directly with always-on assistants like Meta's Muse agent. Anthropic itself says Duet can still misjudge what's urgent, so whether it saves time depends on how much of its work you have to check.

stories.title: Claude proves 239 entry points across 123 open-source libraries crash-free, finding hundreds of bugs
stories.dek: In research published October 22, Anthropic's Frontier Red Team and Theorem had Claude write Rocq proofs about compiled RISC-V binaries. The proofs show that fuzz-test entry points can't crash on any input under 64 MB, under stated assumptions. Along the way Claude found and patched hundreds of bugs, including a decompressor out-of-bounds write and a rediscovered libexpat CVE. The project produced about 180M lines of Rocq. Opus 5.5 needed about 40% fewer tokens than Opus 5 on a 36-task subset.
stories.whyItMatters: Formal verification used to take years of expert work per project, and this suggests it can now scale. It's still expensive (often hundreds of millions of tokens per project), and the guarantees only hold in a simplified single-threaded, static-musl environment.

stories.title: Meta's Muse Wonder Full ties Sonnet 5.5 at 56 on the AA index
stories.dek: Meta announced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on October 12. On AA Intelligence Index v4.3 at max effort, Wonder Full scores 56 and Wonder scores 52, up from Muse Spark 1.3's 48. Wonder Full went from 33% to 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, ranks #2 on GDPval-AA (1857 Elo), and cut its hallucination rate from 33% to 23%, though it still trails on AA-Omniscience knowledge (30). Muse Wonder costs $4/$20 per million tokens on Meta's API. Wonder Full is only available in Muse Code, from $50 a month.
stories.whyItMatters: Meta now has a frontier-class model, but its best version isn't on a per-token API, so most developers can only use the 52-point Wonder.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Argon is generally available, at an introductory $2/$10 per million tokens
stories.dek: Google's Gemini API changelog lists `gemini-4-argon` as generally available as of October 13, after a September 30 launch limited to cyber defenders. It has a 1,048,576-token context window shared by input, thinking, and output, and it's rolling out to Gemini app AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and AI Mode in Search. Artificial Analysis scores it 53 at high effort, tied with GPT-6 Astra, with the lowest hallucination rate (15%) among models scoring 45 or more. Introductory pricing of $2/$10 rises to $4/$20 around December 1.
stories.whyItMatters: Google is back among the top labs, and it's the cheapest model at this tier until the promotion ends. Its DeepSWE 77.9% is self-reported and measured on a different harness, so wait for independent numbers.

stories.title: China-aligned Storm-0940 used the ARTEX agentic pentest framework in a ConnectWise supply-chain attack
stories.dek: Microsoft says Storm-0940 compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application identities, then used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM pentest framework, to sign in to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants without any user sign-in. In some tenants the agents ran Graph reconnaissance, added app credentials, assigned Global Admin, and bulk-read Key Vault secrets. In several cases privileged access came less than three hours after initial targeting. It followed a password-spray campaign (Oct 10–14) with 151,000+ failed logons.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a documented case of autonomous agents running a real intrusion at machine speed. Microsoft's guidance: inventory the affected app IDs, review service-principal sign-ins back to October 1, and preserve evidence before deleting apps.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly raising up to $30B at a $1.25T pre-money valuation
stories.dek: Citing CNBC and Bloomberg, TechCrunch reports that Coatue is leading the round with UAE investors, and that the UAE money may be tied to a compute deal. That's below the $1.4T Bloomberg cited a month ago, and terms are still being negotiated. OpenAI filed confidentially for an IPO in June but is raising privately for now; its March round valued it at $852B post-money. CNBC separately reports Anthropic is seeking a $1.5–2T valuation for its own IPO.
stories.whyItMatters: Both leading labs are heading toward public markets at trillion-dollar valuations. Their compute deals and pricing will increasingly answer to public investors.

modelsMeta.note: Board rebuilt October 5. Since the last refresh, Artificial Analysis moved to Intelligence Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, both on much lower absolute scales (Claude Opus 5 went from 61 to 51 on AA). So every row now uses the current versions; the old numbers aren't comparable. New this cycle: Claude Opus 5.5 (the new AA #1 at 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.7. Grok 4.6's AA score is derived from AA's statement that Grok 4.7 scored +2 over it. DeepSWE figures come from BenchLM's aggregation (last updated Sep 1), plus Opus 5.5's 74.2 from BenchLM's head-to-head. Gemini 4 Argon is not listed yet because it has no independent scores. Older models no longer near the frontier (Opus 4.8, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash) were dropped because they lack v4.3 / CursorBench 4.0 scores. October 7: added Mistral Large 4 (AA 38, research preview Oct 6); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Reflection's Beam is not listed because it has only self-reported scores. October 8: added Claude Haiku 5.5 (AA 43 at max effort, released Oct 7); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. October 24: added Muse Wonder Full (AA 56) and Muse Wonder (AA 52), both released Oct 12; Kimi K3.1 Pro (AA 55, Oct 23); and Gemini 4 Argon (AA 53, generally available Oct 13). Argon was previously held back for lacking independent scores. None of them has a CursorBench 4.0 or BenchLM DeepSWE score yet (BenchLM CursorBench updated Oct 23; DeepSWE still Sep 1). Google's self-reported DeepSWE 77.9% for Argon is not listed because it was run on a different harness.

harness.notes: 2.1.310 brings the Monitor tool and plugin monitors to Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, adds Cloud sessions and Remote Control permissions to Enterprise custom roles, and fixes requests failing behind gateways that reject the `effort-2025-11-24` beta value. 2.1.309 (Oct 22) runs `sed -i` with the standard Bash prompt, makes `claude ultrareview` require workspace trust (`--trust-workspace` for scripts), makes bypass-permissions mode in Desktop and VS Code deny dangerous `rm`/`rmdir` immediately, and fixes sandboxed Bash running shell startup files outside the sandbox. 2.1.307 (Oct 21) added `/claude-api api-version` for migrating to API version `2026-10-21`, a `claude_code.safety_event` OTel event, and `@claude review stop` for Code Review.

Adds ten numbered `/presets` slots for reusable prompts and slash commands, and inline arguments for `/model` and `/permissions` (model, reasoning effort, speed, permission profile). Images show in the fullscreen transcript on Kitty and Sixel terminals. Enterprise MCP connections can authenticate with Codex account grants or a dedicated sign-in, including OAuth clients that need secrets. Credentials are masked in supported remote Bash and Zsh snapshot sessions, and the Bedrock setup wizard is on by default. Fixes: failed compaction no longer leaves partial summaries, resumed sessions keep their thread settings, and Windows proxy auth works with Negotiate/NTLM. 0.165.0 alphas have started.

Parallel codemode scripts and in-process subagents now queue for a free worker instead of failing (raise the limit with `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS`). Compaction and branch summaries use the model's own output limit, so long reasoning no longer breaks them. New generated Models Configuration reference for `models.json`; classifier image input for TypeSafe Jev and Cloudflare Clef; Rex terminal support. Earlier: 1.3.0 (Oct 15) added a `sessionShareDestination` setting for `/share` and keeps the prompt cache when you change the thinking level on GPT-6; 1.2.0 (Oct 12) added per-key OpenRouter model lists and published `$schema` files for its config.

extensions.name: Hedera Network MCP
extensions.blurb: A hosted, OAuth 2.1 MCP endpoint with 40+ Hedera testnet tools (HBAR transfers, token create/mint/airdrop, consensus topics, mirror-node queries) for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and ChatGPT. Agents can propose transactions, but every state-changing call waits for you to sign in your own wallet. It's a useful reference design for human-in-the-loop write tools. Testnet only, with no spend caps yet.

extensions.name: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
extensions.blurb: An MIT-licensed MCP server that lets coding agents analyze native binaries, JS/Electron apps, .NET assemblies, APKs, firmware, and HAR captures, using Ghidra, Hopper, or IDA for native code. `npx rea-agents setup` wires it into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and others. It isn't a sandbox, so only point it at binaries you trust.

extensions.name: MCP Registry census (Oct 2026)
extensions.blurb: A mid-October survey of the official MCP Registry counts 43,012 active servers, and finds 78% of servers first published in October expose a remote URL. Hosted, OAuth-authenticated servers like Hedera's are becoming the norm over local stdio installs. The figures come from one person's sampling.

tips.title: Save your go-to prompts in /presets slots
tips.body: Codex 0.164.0 gives you ten numbered `/presets` slots with a keyboard menu. Store your review checklist, a 'write tests first' instruction, or a long slash command once and recall it in a keystroke. Pair it with the new inline arguments to switch model, reasoning effort, and permission profile in one line instead of clicking through menus.

tips.title: Fan out codemode subagents without hitting worker errors
tips.body: Since Pi 1.4.0, parallel codemode scripts and in-process subagents queue when all workers are busy instead of failing. That makes big fan-outs (one subagent per file or per package) safe to launch. If you have the cores and API headroom, raise the ceiling with `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS`.

tips.title: Migrate Claude API code to the new 2026-10-21 version with one command
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.307 adds `/claude-api api-version`, which updates your Claude API code to API version `2026-10-21`. As of 2.1.309, the `/claude-api` skill builds Managed Agents subagent teams on `multiagent_20261001`. Run it on a branch and review the diff, rather than editing headers and tool types by hand.
